title.narrative: Voices Unheard from Pyrenees to Kibera

description.narrative:
Our project addresses youth underrepresentation in climate policy-making, focusing on marginalized communities in the French Pyrenees and Kibera slum in Nairobi, Kenya. Both regions face severe climate-induced disasters: in the Pyrenees, rural communities experience floods, droughts, and wildfires threatening their socio-economic viability; in Kibera, intense rainfall frequently causes severeflooding, worsened by inadequate sewage infrastructure, as seen in the deadly 2024 floods. Through targeted policy advocacy, our project empowers young people (18-35) from these communities to engage directly with policymakers at local, national, and international levels, allowing them to share lived experiences, voice critical needs, and propose adaptation solutions.
Our strategy combines grassroots research, evidence-based advocacy, and intercontinental youth-led policy dialogue to influence climate adaptation policies, amplify marginalized voices, and foster cross-regional knowledge exchange between Europe andAfrica. Participants will engage directly with policymakers from the European Commission, African Union, local governments, and NGO working in this area through dialogues, webinars, and field visits. By documenting their experiences and advocating for keypolicy recommendations - such as improved infrastructure in Kibera and climate adaptation training in the Pyrenees - the project will raise awareness among policymakers and enhance preparedness and climate resilience in these marginalized communities.
The project contributes to SDG 13 (Climate Action) by equipping marginalized youth with advocacy tools to promote effective climate adaptation. It aligns with SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) by enhancing urban and rural resilience, focusing on infrastructure improvements in Kibera and adaptation to climate catastrophes. Additionally, it supports SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) by addressing Kibera’s sewage system challenges and improving access to safe and hygienic sanitation facilities. Finally, SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) is at the core of our project, fostering EU-AU cooperation through cross-border youth collaboration, policy engagement, and long-term institutional partnerships.

participating-org.narrative:
Association Petite Graine envisions empowered youth actively contributing to sustainable development, creating resilient communities aligned with the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
APG aims to educate and engage young people, especially those from rural and marginalized backgrounds, by equipping them with skills and knowledge necessary for active participation in sustainable development efforts. The organization emphasizes climate action (SDG 13), social inclusion, and digital literacy.
Objectives: - Raise awareness of all 17 SDGs among youth, linking global challenges to local contexts. - Empower youth through practical skill-building in communication, collaboration, leadership, and problem-solving. - Create accessible digital educational resources for sustainability education. - Foster partnerships for greater local, national, and international impact.
APG is driven by inclusivity, active citizenship, sustainability, collaboration, and innovation, ensuring meaningfulyouth empowerment and long-term community engagement in environmental action.
Association Petite Graine (APG) operates under a governance structure of non-profit organizations, with a board that provides overall strategic direction and oversight. Thisincludes roles such as President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, and project coordinators. APG maintains a flat, participatory governance approach, actively involving young people, volunteers, and professionals in decision-making processes. The board ensures compliance with organizational goals and oversees the implementation of educational and sustainability projects aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). APG emphasizes collaborative decision-making, actively involving young people and volunteers in project design and execution. The team leverages its diverse expertise in non-formal education, climate action, digital outreach, and policy advocacy to engage marginalized communities effectively.
